fixes.answer: Food is absolutely central to culture, in my view. It is far more than mere [[sustenance]]; it reflects a nation's history, geography, values and social customs. Sharing a meal is a universal expression of hospitality and community. Traditional dishes carry deep [[sentimental]] and cultural significance, passed down through generations. So I would say cuisine is one of the most [[tangible]] and beloved expressions of a country's identity.

Eating habits have changed considerably. In the past, people mostly ate home-cooked, seasonal and local food, often together as a family. Today, busy lifestyles have led to more processed food, takeaways and eating [[on the go]], often alone. [[Portion sizes]] have grown, and international cuisine is now widely available. While this offers more variety and convenience, I think it has come at some cost to health and the [[communal]] nature of dining.
fixes.why: 'health' and 'dining' are plain; marked 'on the go' and 'portion sizes'

fixes.answer: Its popularity comes down to a few key factors. Firstly, it is convenient and quick, which suits our increasingly busy, time-poor lifestyles. Secondly, it is relatively cheap and consistently tasty, engineered to appeal to our [[cravings]]. Aggressive marketing has also made it [[ubiquitous]] and aspirational. Unfortunately, this convenience comes at a cost, as many argue its popularity has contributed to rising rates of [[obesity]] and related health problems.
fixes.why: 'problems' is plain; marked 'cravings'; softened the obesity claim

fixes.answer: It has a mixed effect. On the positive side, it enriches our [[culinary]] options and promotes [[cultural exchange]], allowing people to enjoy dishes from around the world. This is broadening and enjoyable. However, there is a concern that the popularity of international chains could [[overshadow]] and threaten traditional local cuisine. So while it adds welcome diversity, it is important that local food traditions are also valued and preserved alongside it.
fixes.why: 'diversity' and 'preserved' are plain; marked 'culinary' and 'cultural exchange'

fixes.answer: I anticipate significant changes driven by health and sustainability concerns. Plant-based diets and [[alternative proteins]], like lab-grown meat, are likely to become far more [[mainstream]] as we address the environmental impact of food. Technology may also personalise nutrition. Hopefully, there will be a renewed appreciation for healthy, [[sustainable]] eating. So our diets may become more conscious and innovative, balancing convenience with health and the planet.
fixes.why: 'conscious' and 'innovative' are plain; marked 'alternative proteins' and 'mainstream'

fixes.answer: A range of measures could help. Education about nutrition from a young age is fundamental, so people can make informed choices. Making healthy food more affordable and accessible, while perhaps [[taxing unhealthy options]], can shift behaviour. Clear [[food labelling]] and restrictions on junk food advertising, especially to children, would also help. Ultimately, creating an environment where the healthy choice is the easy, [[appealing]] choice is the most effective approach.
fixes.why: 'effective' and 'approach' are plain; marked 'taxing unhealthy options' and 'food labelling'

fixes.answer: Eating out offers convenience, saves time on cooking and cleaning, and provides a pleasant social experience and variety. It can be [[a real treat]]. The disadvantages, however, are that it is expensive and often less healthy, as restaurant food tends to be higher in salt, sugar and fat, with larger portions. Doing it too often can [[strain]] both your finances and your health. So it is best enjoyed in [[moderation]].
fixes.why: 'finances' and 'health' are plain; marked 'a real treat' and 'strain'

fixes.answer: I largely agree, particularly regarding health and value. Home cooking allows you to control the ingredients, ensuring meals are fresher, healthier and cheaper, and it can be a rewarding activity. There is also something uniquely [[comforting]] about a home-cooked meal. However, I would not say it is always better; skilled chefs create [[exquisite]] dishes that are hard to [[replicate]] at home. So home cooking is generally healthier, but restaurants offer expertise and occasion.
